## The vignette runs when the parameter file is available: either the release
## asset (load_model() downloads it) or a local copy given in FINNMODELBWI_PARAMETERS.
local_pt <- Sys.getenv("FINNMODELBWI_PARAMETERS", unset = "")
can_run <- nzchar(local_pt) || nzchar(FINNmodelBWI::model_info()[[1]]$url)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = can_run)
```

## 1. Load the model

The package ships the model *definition* (`build_model()`) and the release
metadata; the fitted parameters are a small file (`parameters.pt`, a named list
of parameter tensors) that `load_model()` downloads once and checks against its
sha256. The model is rebuilt with the installed FINN (0.2.0 or later).

```{r load}
library(FINNmodelBWI)
library(FINN)
library(torch)
torch_set_num_threads(1L)
m <- if (nzchar(local_pt)) load_model(path = local_pt) else load_model()
species_table()
```

## 2. The inputs: five covariates, natural units

`covariate_table()` says where each covariate comes from and how to derive it
for a new site. Two of them are *settings* rather than measurements:

* `management`: the regular-harvest tier of the stand, 0 (no harvest), 1
  (up to 5 % of the start basal area removed per decade), 2 (5-20 %) or 3
  (more than 20 %). It shifts growth, mortality and recruitment by
  species-specific slopes. In the calibration it is derived from the same
  decade's removals, so treat it as a sensitivity: report results over tiers
  0 to 3 rather than for one tier.
* `drought2`: the two-year soil-moisture anomaly, 0 = average year, about -1 =
  a dry year like 2003 or 2018 at most German sites, -1.5 to -2.3 = the driest
  site-years of the calibration. Env row `k` drives simulated year `k + 1`.

`scale_env()` applies the model's scaling constants (one mean and sd per
covariate, pooled over the calibration data).

```{r covariates}
covariate_table()[, c("name", "unit")]
```

## 3. Synthetic example stands under two management tiers

The stands below are **synthetic**: four typical German stand types with
diameters and stem numbers chosen by hand (stems per 0.1 ha patch), on one
mid-elevation site with an average decade and a dry 2018-2020 (`drought2`
-1.2, -1.5, -1.0 in years 7-9). Section 4 uses real inventory stands.

```{r example}
sp <- function(name) species_table()$species[species_table()$name == name]
stands <- list(
  spruce        = data.frame(species = sp("Picea abies"),      dbh = c(45, 35, 25, 15), trees = c(8, 14, 18, 10)),
  beech         = data.frame(species = sp("Fagus sylvatica"),  dbh = c(55, 40, 28, 16), trees = c(5, 9, 14, 20)),
  pine_birch    = data.frame(species = c(rep(sp("Pinus sylvestris"), 3), sp("Betula pendula")), dbh = c(38, 30, 22, 14), trees = c(12, 18, 16, 10)),
  oak_hornbeam  = data.frame(species = c(rep(sp("Quercus petraea"), 3), sp("Carpinus betulus")), dbh = c(50, 36, 24, 12), trees = c(6, 10, 12, 25)))
init <- data.table::rbindlist(lapply(seq_along(stands), function(i) cbind(siteID = i, patchID = 1L, stands[[i]])))
init[, treeName := paste(siteID, species, dbh, sep = "_")]
init_cohort <- makeInitCohorts(init, Nspecies = nrow(species_table()))

env <- data.table::CJ(siteID = seq_along(stands), year = 0:10)
env[, `:=`(mat_c = 8.0, map_mm = 800, elev_m = 400, management = 0,
           drought2 = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, -1.2, -1.5, -1.0, 0)[year + 1])]

run <- function(tier) {
  e <- data.table::copy(env)[, management := tier]
  FINN.seed(1)
  s <- simulateForest(m, env = scale_env(e), init_cohort = init_cohort, patch_size = 0.1, device = "cpu")$wide$site
  s <- as.data.frame(lapply(s, function(x) if (is.factor(x)) as.integer(as.character(x)) else x))
  aggregate(cbind(ba_ha = ba / 0.1, stems_ha = trees / 0.1) ~ siteID + year, s, sum)
}
tier0 <- run(0)
tier3 <- run(3)
start <- tier0[tier0$year == 1, c("siteID", "ba_ha")]
end   <- function(x) x[x$year == 11, "ba_ha"]
data.frame(stand = names(stands), ba_start = round(start$ba_ha, 1), ba_tier0 = round(end(tier0), 1), ba_tier3 = round(end(tier3), 1))
```

```{r plot-example}
plot(NA, xlim = c(1, 11), ylim = c(0, max(tier0$ba_ha) * 1.05), xlab = "simulated year", ylab = "basal area (m2/ha)")
for (s in seq_along(stands)) {
  lines(ba_ha ~ year, tier0[tier0$siteID == s, ], col = s, lwd = 2)
  lines(ba_ha ~ year, tier3[tier3$siteID == s, ], col = s, lwd = 2, lty = 2)
}
legend("bottomleft", c(names(stands), "tier 0 (no harvest)", "tier 3 (> 20 %/decade)"),
       col = c(seq_along(stands), 1, 1), lty = c(rep(1, 4), 1, 2), lwd = 2, bty = "n", ncol = 2)
```

## 4. Real BWI example stands

Four holdout corners of the inventory (never used in the fit) ship with the
package (`inst/extdata`, CC BY-SA 4.0 with attribution to the Thünen
Institute, see `LICENSE-parameters.md`): their 2012 stand, environment in
natural units and the observed 2012-2022 drought index; positions as 1 km
INSPIRE cells rounded to 0.05 degrees, no identifiers. The decade as observed
(management tiers 0, 0, 3, 2) and with every site at tier 0 and tier 3.
`calibration/09_example_sites.R` of the model repository rebuilds such stands
from the prepared data.

```{r real}
env_r  <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "example_env.csv",  package = "FINNmodelBWI"))
init_r <- data.table::fread(system.file("extdata", "example_init.csv", package = "FINNmodelBWI"))   # makeInitCohorts() wants a data.table
init_r[, treeName := paste(siteID, species, dbh, .I, sep = "_")]
ic_r <- makeInitCohorts(init_r, Nspecies = nrow(species_table()))
run_r <- function(tier = NULL) {
  e <- env_r
  if (!is.null(tier)) e$management <- tier
  FINN.seed(1)
  s <- simulateForest(m, env = scale_env(e), init_cohort = ic_r, patch_size = 0.1, device = "cpu")$wide$site
  s <- as.data.frame(lapply(s, function(x) if (is.factor(x)) as.integer(as.character(x)) else x))
  aggregate(cbind(ba_ha = ba / 0.1) ~ siteID + year, s, sum)
}
rec <- run_r(); r0 <- run_r(0); r3 <- run_r(3)
dominant <- sapply(split(init_r, init_r$siteID), function(d) names(which.max(tapply(d$trees * d$dbh^2, d$species_name, sum))))
data.frame(site = 1:4, dominant = dominant, tier_recorded = env_r$management[env_r$year == 0],
           ba_start = round(r0$ba_ha[r0$year == 1], 1), ba_recorded = round(rec$ba_ha[rec$year == 11], 1),
           ba_tier0 = round(r0$ba_ha[r0$year == 11], 1), ba_tier3 = round(r3$ba_ha[r3$year == 11], 1))
```

## 5. A drought scenario

Set `drought2` directly: here an average climate with a three-year drought of
-1.5 sd in years 5-7, at a mid-elevation site, from bare ground (20 patches).

```{r drought}
site <- data.frame(siteID = 1L, year = 0:40, mat_c = 7.5, map_mm = 850, elev_m = 450, management = 0)
site$drought2 <- ifelse(site$year %in% 5:7, -1.5, 0)
FINN.seed(2)
bare <- simulateForest(m, env = scale_env(site), init_cohort = NULL, patches = 20L, patch_size = 0.1, device = "cpu")$wide$site
bare <- as.data.frame(lapply(bare, function(x) if (is.factor(x)) as.integer(as.character(x)) else x))
tot <- aggregate(cbind(ba_ha = ba / 0.1) ~ year, bare, sum)
top <- aggregate(ba ~ species, bare[bare$year == 40, ], sum)
merge(top[order(-top$ba), ][1:4, ], species_table(), by = "species")
plot(ba_ha ~ year, tot, type = "l", lwd = 2, xlab = "year", ylab = "basal area (m2/ha)", main = "bare ground, drought in years 5-7")
abline(v = c(5, 7), lty = 3)
```

## 6. What to keep in mind

* Units: `dbh` in cm, `ba` in m2 and `trees` as stems **per 0.1 ha patch**
  (divide by 0.1 for per hectare); `growth` is the relative diameter increment
  per year; `mort` the annual removal probability; `r_mean_ha` recruits per ha.
* Recruits enter at 7 cm dbh (the inventory's caliper threshold). The
  recruitment level is about twice the ingrowth that the angle-count sample
  implies for the first decade (a documented choice of the data preparation,
  see the model card), so stem numbers of small trees run high.
* The model has no density-dependent mortality beyond light competition and no
  bark-beetle process; long bare-ground runs settle at 40-45 m2/ha dominated
  by beech, and the drought response is a logit-linear extrapolation beyond
  `drought2` of about -2.3.
* Mortality means *removal* (natural death plus harvest). The management tier
  does not cut trees; it raises the removal rate.
```
